query: Which material can be used for enhanced catalytic activity and durability toward HER and HOR, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A Pt-Ni alloy structured as a core‐shell nanoparticle—with a Pt-rich shell and a Ni-rich core—can enhance both the catalytic activity and durability for HER and HOR relative to conventional pure Pt catalysts.
generation.material_initial_state: Conventional pure Pt nanoparticles typically used for HER/HOR applications.
generation.intervention: Synthesize Pt-Ni core–shell nanoparticles that ensure a Pt-enriched outer layer while incorporating a Ni-rich core.
generation.conditions: Electrochemical testing in acidic electrolytes (e.g., 0.1 M HClO4) at ambient temperature under standard HER/HOR cycling conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: The core–shell nanostructure, which modifies the surface electronic structure due to alloying, leading to an optimal hydrogen binding energy.
generation.mechanism: The incorporation of Ni is expected to shift the d-band center of the Pt surface, adjusting the hydrogen adsorption energy to a more favorable level for both HER and HOR kinetics. The core–shell design also helps protect the less noble Ni from dissolution, thereby enhancing durability under cycling conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in the overpotential and an increase in current density for HER/HOR, combined with improved stability over long-term cycling compared to pure Pt nanoparticles.
generation.baseline: Published performance metrics of conventional pure Pt catalysts measured under identical experimental conditions.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to acidic environments, and the exact improvements may vary with particle size, synthesis conditions, and the exact Pt:Ni ratio. Performance in alkaline conditions may not replicate the same outcomes.
generation.uncertainty: While the theoretical mechanisms suggest improved activity and durability, the quantitative extent of improvement is uncertain due to synthesis complexities and system variations.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare and characterize samples of both pure Pt nanoparticles and the engineered Pt-Ni core–shell nanoparticles. Subject both materials to identical electrochemical testing protocols in an acidic electrolyte, recording overpotential, current density, and stability over multiple cycling periods.
measurements: Overpotential at a defined current density for HER/HOR
Durability metrics based on performance drop over extended cycling
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Pt-Ni core–shell nanoparticles do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in both lower overpotential/higher current density and enhanced durability compared to the pure Pt nanoparticles under the identical conditions, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
